name: Londoner Grand, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Macao
detail: The Londoner Hotel Macau, located in the heart of the Cotai Strip, impresses with its London-themed interior, creating a strong classic atmosphere from the lobby. The check-in staff are very friendly and actively assist with luggage handling, restaurant reservations, etc., leaving a good first impression. The rooms are spacious suites, among the largest in Macau, with separate bedrooms, living rooms, and dressing rooms ensuring good privacy during your stay. The bedding is plush, and the linen quality is excellent, guaranteeing a good night's sleep. The marble bathroom is well-equipped with a rain shower, bathtub, and two sinks for convenience. The amenities, including a capsule coffee machine and a premium tea set, were also satisfying. The facilities are abundant, featuring both indoor and outdoor pools, a sauna, steam room, and fitness center. The breakfast offers a variety of options from Western to Asian cuisine, making the overnight rate worthwhile. There are many shops and restaurants within the hotel, and it's advantageous that you can access the Venetian and Parisian through connecting corridors, avoiding the weather. However, due to the large size of the hotel, there can be wait times during peak check-in and check-out hours, and restaurant and room service prices are relatively high. Nevertheless, the **service, space, and convenience are all outstanding, making it a highly recommended hotel for those planning a special trip.**

name: The Parisian Macao
detail: There is a free shuttle bus to the airport, Taipa area, and affiliated hotels, which is convenient. I was impressed by the luxurious reception and friendly staff. The breakfast was diverse and the bread and sweets were exquisite. The clean room had a bathtub and the view of the Eiffel Tower was also excellent. The hotel was enveloped in a pleasant aroma, had many photogenic spots, and I was able to spend a quiet and comfortable time.

name: The Venetian Macao
detail: The exterior and interior were both very beautiful, and my mood elevated instantly upon arrival. The room was just as shown in the pictures, so spacious that it felt like a waste to use it for just one person, allowing me to relax comfortably. I had informed them prior to my stay that it was for my birthday, and they kindly confirmed the type of cake and the timing for serving it. On the day, they provided a lovely birthday cake that was not only visually beautiful but also very delicious. I received a congratulatory message during check-in, and the heartfelt service left a strong impression. Additionally, I arrived earlier than the check-in time, but they accommodatingly and flexibly handled this, which I greatly appreciated. The pool was also excellent; since it was a slightly chilly day, I chose not to go into the water and was relaxing when a staff member guided me to the jacuzzi, allowing me to enjoy a comfortable warm experience. They even provided fruits, which was a delightful touch of detailed service. The facility also has a shopping mall, which added to my enjoyment during the stay. This is a wonderful hotel that I would definitely like to use again when I visit Macau.

name: Hotel Royal Macau
detail: Travel with elders in a relaxed local manner, with city center locations where you can walk to attractions in 5-10 minutes. There are many authentic food markets nearby, offering Chinese, Portuguese, Thai, Myanmar, and vegetarian options. Facilities include a swimming pool and gym, as well as a cake shop, making it suitable for those looking for a simple short vacation. The rooms are relatively simple and small, but have a nice view, with local traditional parks and the Taishi small market held regularly. Seniors appreciate the quietness and convenience, making it very appropriate! I would choose the Royal Hotel again if given the opportunity!

name: Hotel Golden Dragon
detail: On the last day of my trip to Hong Kong, I decided to stay suddenly and was able to find a cheap last-minute rate. It’s just a short walk from the ferry terminal in Sheung Wan if you use the second-floor walkway. The hotel is very luxurious and beautiful. There was a casino inside with only slot machines. There seemed to be a gym, but it was closed at night, so I couldn't use it. When I asked for ice, they delivered it to my room for free. I was able to communicate even with broken English, and I left my luggage at the front desk and received information about the bus stop for the local buses. I took bus number 3 to and from Senado Square, and it was convenient to catch the number 102 bus directly next to the hotel to the airport bus stop. It was a perfect distance for a walk to the coast, and there is a supermarket nearby. Although it's a bit far from the city, it was quiet and very nice.

name: Regency Art Hotel
detail: At this price point, the service and cleanliness are really good, the sound insulation is okay, but if you're facing the street, there will be some noise from cars. If you're really sensitive to that, it's better not to choose a street-facing room or wearing earplugs is also fine. Overall, it's clean and tidy. The room is spacious, and everything you need is available. The bed is comfortable, and the self-service breakfast is just over 90 dollars. Although the variety is not that many, it caters to the general taste. It’s worth the price. If I go to Macau again, I would still choose this hotel. The service is really good, everyone is friendly, and it's very convenient for luggage storage and calling a taxi. Taking a taxi to attractions outside is very fast; it was a really good experience.

name: Vo Peng Hostel
detail: Geographic location: Very close to Ruins of St. Paul's, you can walk there, and it's also within walking distance from attractions like the New Lisboa and Wynn. Excellent location. Rooms: There are single and double rooms, overall quite clean and hygienic, without noise, and I slept very soundly. Price: Super great. Service attitude: The owner is very patient, provides thoughtful service, speaks politely, and is responsive to requests. Next time I go to Macau, I will stay here again.

name: Grandview Hotel
detail: I stayed for a concert, and the access to the bus stop and station was good. I was able to walk to Rua do Cunha, which allowed me to enjoy Macau. There were also restaurants, supermarkets, and convenience stores nearby, so I didn't feel any inconvenience. I also thought the area was safe even when I went out at night. The water facilities were clean, and they provided cleaning services every day, so I didn't have any issues. Many of the staff at the reception spoke English, and everyone was friendly!

name: Fu Hua Hotel
detail: This trip to Macau with the elderly and children, staying at the Fu Hua Hotel, was a wonderful experience. It is very close to the Ruins of St. Paul's, making it easy to stroll around the historical district during the day and enjoy the night scenery in the evening, without tiring the elderly or children. Public transport during holidays is also very convenient, with nearby bus stops and frequent services, so there’s no need to worry about transportation. The hotel service is warm, the rooms are clean and quiet, and the surrounding area is convenient for daily needs, making it an ideal choice for exploring the old district. I highly recommend it for family travel!

name: City Viva Hotel Macau
detail: It was my first trip to Macau, and I was able to relax very comfortably during my stay at this hotel. I arrived at the Outer Harbor from Hong Kong by turbojet and walked to the hotel in about 10 minutes while enjoying the atmosphere of the town. I could also take a leisurely walk to nearby famous tourist spots, and there were delicious Chinese restaurants around the hotel, which made me very satisfied. The hotel room was clean, and I felt the luxuriousness unique to Macau, which made me very happy. I would like to stay at this hotel again when I travel to Macau.
